pairs: Visio qua erudivit eum mater sua.
The vision by which his mother instructed him:
Do not give your substance to women,
et divitias tuas ad delendos reges.
or your riches to overthrow kings.
quia nullum secretum est ubi regnat ebrietas;
For there are no secrets where drunkenness reigns.
and alter the case of the sons of the poor.
Give strong drink to the grieving,
et vinum his qui amaro sunt animo.
and wine to those who are bitter in soul.
et doloris sui non recordentur amplius.
and remember their sorrow no more.
Open your mouth for the mute
et causis omnium filiorum qui pertranseunt.
and for all the cases of the sons who are passing through.
and do justice to the indigent and the poor.
Who shall find a strong woman?
procul et de ultimis finibus pretium ejus.
Far away, and from the furthest parts, is her price.
Confidit in ea cor viri sui,
The heart of her husband confides in her,
and he will not be deprived of spoils.
She will repay him with good,
all the days of her life.
She has sought wool and flax,
et operata est consilia manuum suarum.
and she has worked these by the counsel of her hands.
She has become like a merchant’s ship,
bringing her bread from far away.
And she has risen in the night,
and given a prey to her household,
She has considered a field and bought it.
From the fruit of her own hands,
de fructu manuum suarum plantavit vineam.
She has wrapped her waist with fortitude,
and she has strengthened her arm.
et vidit quia bona est negotiatio ejus;
and seen that her tasks are good;
non extinguetur in nocte lucerna ejus.
her lamp shall not be extinguished at night.
She has put her hand to strong things,
and her fingers have taken hold of the spindle.
She has opened her hand to the needy,
et palmas suas extendit ad pauperem.
and she has extended her hands to the poor.
Non timebit domui suæ a frigoribus nivis;
She shall not fear, in the cold of snow, for her household.
omnes enim domestici ejus vestiti sunt duplicibus.
For all those of her household have been clothed two-fold.
She has made embroidered clothing for herself.
Fine linen and purple is her garment.
Her husband is noble at the gates,
when he sits among the senators of the land.
She has made finely woven cloth
and she has delivered a waistband to the Canaanite.
Strength and elegance are her clothing,
and she will laugh in the final days.
She has opened her mouth to wisdom,
et lex clementiæ in lingua ejus.
and the law of clemency is on her tongue.
She has considered the paths of her household,
and she has not eaten her bread in idleness.
Many daughters have gathered together riches;
The woman who fears the Lord,
Date ei de fructu manuum suarum,
Give to her from the fruit of her own hands.
et laudent eam in portis opera ejus.
And let her works praise her at the gates.
